title: ⭐⭐ Revision: gifts, types and a description

questions.prompt: Nour uses the verb navigate about the internet, not about a boat. What does she mean by it?

options.text: that she builds a new page for a website
that she finds her way from page to page
that she sails across a very wide sea
that she teaches others how to use a computer

questions.explanation: "that she finds her way from page to page" is the meaning: to navigate is to find your way, and on the internet the sea becomes a set of pages. "that she sails across a very wide sea" is the older meaning, the one she says she is not using. "that she builds a new page for a website" would be to create, and "that she teaches others how to use a computer" would be to train somebody, neither of which is finding a way.

questions.prompt: Slim writes about a gifted neighbour: "He is nineteen, tall and thin, and his father is a fisherman." Which three kinds of detail has he given?

options.text: physical appearance, hobbies and social background
age, physical appearance and school results
age, physical appearance and social background
name, age and physical appearance

questions.explanation: "age, physical appearance and social background" is the right list: nineteen gives the age, tall and thin the appearance, and the father's trade the background the neighbour comes from. "age, physical appearance and school results" invents marks that are not in the sentence, "name, age and physical appearance" counts a name Slim never writes, and "physical appearance, hobbies and social background" replaces the age with hobbies nobody mentions.

questions.prompt: You are writing an acrostic on the word PUPILS and you need its first line. Which of these can open it?

options.text: I always play music with my friends
Playing music with my friends
Pupils play music with friends
The pupils are playing music together

questions.explanation: "Playing music with my friends" is the one: it opens with the letter P, the first letter of PUPILS, and with a verb in the -ing form, which is what every line of the model poem does. "Pupils play music with friends" starts with the right letter but with a conjugated verb, and it writes the word the poem is supposed to hide. "I always play music with my friends" and "The pupils are playing music together" both start with the wrong letter.

questions.prompt: Amira understands a rule the first time it is explained to her. Which sentence says so in correct English?

options.text: Amira has gifted at understanding a new rule.
Amira is a gift at understanding a new rule.
Amira is a prodigy of understanding a new rule.
Amira is gifted at understanding a new rule.

questions.explanation: "Amira is gifted at understanding a new rule." is correct: gifted is an adjective, so it follows the verb to be, and it takes at before an activity. "Amira has gifted at understanding a new rule." uses that adjective as if it were a noun. "Amira is a gift at understanding a new rule." turns the girl into the ability itself, and "Amira is a prodigy of understanding a new rule." uses a word reserved for a very young person with an astonishing ability, with a preposition that does not follow it.

questions.prompt: Wassim gets average marks, but he can mend anything in the house and he explains each repair clearly to his little brother. A neighbour says he is not intelligent. What does the lesson answer?

options.text: He will become intelligent when his marks improve.
School marks are the only real proof of an intelligence.
There is more than one kind of intelligence, and mending is one of them.
Explaining things clearly to a child is not a sign of intelligence.

questions.explanation: "There is more than one kind of intelligence, and mending is one of them." is the lesson's whole answer: Wassim shows the mechanical type, and the neighbour is judging him on one type only. "School marks are the only real proof of an intelligence." is the narrow definition the first activity asks you to question. "He will become intelligent when his marks improve." keeps the same narrow measure, and "Explaining things clearly to a child is not a sign of intelligence." throws away a second sign, since making somebody else understand is itself a gift.

questions.prompt: You must organise everything you have collected into one description of a gifted person. Which plan follows the lesson?

options.text: what he can do, an example of each, then age, looks and background
his age and his looks only, in one long paragraph
the list of the six types of intelligence, then his name
the poem first, then the questionnaire, then his name

questions.explanation: "what he can do, an example of each, then age, looks and background" is the plan: the statements you chose come first, each one carried by its example, and the three details close the portrait. "his age and his looks only, in one long paragraph" keeps the decoration and drops the subject. "the list of the six types of intelligence, then his name" copies the questionnaire instead of describing anybody, and "the poem first, then the questionnaire, then his name" lines up the activities of the lesson rather than the information they produced.
